title: Solving
description: One solve per problem (decision 0010), named by the problem's id. Starting calls return at once; what happens comes as events. A sliding problem is solved as the original's solve thread did: the assembler finds the start layouts, and each is searched to the goal (decision 0014). A stacking problem too (decision 0015): one search from its start stacking to its goal, its path the one solution; a paused stacking solve is its search saved in the engine's panexFolder, which outlives the run, the document and the engine: solve.continue carries it on (also on a reopened file), solve.start and solve.abort throw it away, solve.status describes it (savedSearch), and the paused solve's export and import carry it.

solve.start.summary: Solves from the start, dropping what the problem holds of earlier solving (a stacking problem's saved search too: the original's Solve asked first, solve.status.savedSearch tells it). Refused (invalid_argument) with the original's message when the problem cannot be solved as it stands (no result, no pieces; a stacking problem without a rod set, with neither disassemble nor justCount, or whose stacks break its rules), and (unsupported) when its grid or solver cannot take it.

solve.prepare.summary: Drops what the problem holds, builds the search (placements, reduce) and pauses. A stacking search has nothing to build (unsupported).

solve.continue.summary: Carries on a paused solve, one saved in the file, a stacking problem's saved search, or an unsolved problem from the start.

solve.pause.summary: Asks the run to pause where it can be continued; nothing is lost. Does not wait: solve.state 'paused' follows. Refused when no run is under way.

solve.savePoint.summary: Asks the assembly search alone to pause where the solve can be saved; the take-aparts under way finish, then 'paused'. The autosave: save, then solve.continue. Refused (unsupported) on a stacking solve, which the original never autosaved: its search saves itself every 20 minutes (StackingOptions.autosave) and when it stops.

solve.abort.summary: The hard stop of a solve under way (a run active, or paused in memory): throws it away (results, paused state, saved position) and waits for the run to end. Refused (invalid_state) when the problem has no such solve, so a finished run's solutions are never lost by a late click: remove them with solution.delete {which: all}, which can be undone; a paused solve from a file is carried on with solve.continue or started over with solve.start. Two document.changed follow: the abort's own, then the run's end from the poll. A stacking problem whose search is saved (solve.status.savedSearch) has a solve under way though no run is in memory, as the original's Abort judged it: the search and the problem's results go, and one document.changed follows.

solve.status.summary: Where the solve stands, its statistics, and why it failed.

note.description: What a sliding or stacking solve's last run said when it was through, or a stacking search when it paused: whether a missing solution is proven, the search gave up at a limit, or where it was saved (the original's solver note, shown in a message box); null otherwise.

oneOf.description: A stacking problem's search saved in the engine's panexFolder: solve.continue carries it on, solve.start and solve.abort throw it away (the original's Solve asked 'This problem has <description>. Continue it, or start over and discard it?').

description.description: e.g. 'a saved search 200 moves deep, 3.4M stackings'.

levelBytes.description: The bytes its levels take (solve.exportPaused withLevels; the original asked about them beyond 1 GB).

savedSearch.description: Null while the problem's run is active, when there is none, and on other grids.

solve.exportPaused.summary: Writes a paused solve as a .slsolve file (the original's BTSOLVE2: the puzzle and the problem's number) to carry it on elsewhere. A stacking problem is paused when its search is saved (solve.status.savedSearch): the file carries the search, packed.

withLevels.description: A stacking search's saved levels go into the file too (default true): left out, the file is far smaller, but finding the path at the end takes longer.

solve.importPaused.summary: Opens a .slsolve file as a new, untitled document (the open one goes as with document.new); solve.continue on the problem carries the solve on. A stacking search it carries goes into its folder in the engine's panexFolder, replacing what was there; without a panexFolder such a file is refused (parse_error), and so is any import (invalid_state) while the open document is a stacking puzzle being solved, whose search would write the same folder as it stops.

solve.state.summary: A solve's state changed, as the engine's poll saw it: states a run passes through within one poll (50 ms) are skipped, the last state of a run (finished, paused, error, or idle after an abort) is always sent, and it comes before the document.changed that gives the run's end its revision. A client waits for that revision, not the state, before reloading the lists. The problems of a document that is replaced get a last 'idle' after the replacing call's reply.

solve.progress.summary: Where a running solve stands; at most four times a second, and once when a run ends (after its last solve.state). The live counters of the Solver card (assemblies, solutions, time) come from here.

solve.solutionsAdded.summary: The saved solutions changed while solving (new ones, or the list thinned or re-sorted): page them again. At most four times a second, and once when the run ends; the last one of a run carries the final count. The counts are those at the time; the live counters are solve.progress's.
